changes: Added packages/main/src/core/runtime-artifact-registry.ts as the single source of truth for runtime artifacts; wired evidence freshness, baseline risk, story dirty filtering, koala init .gitignore merge, and doctor tracked-artifact reporting and repair to it; updated validation smokes and docs; hardened doctor repair command shell quoting after F-001.
usage: Run koala init in an existing project to merge managed runtime ignore rules. Run koala doctor to see tracked runtime artifacts and koala doctor --repair to untrack repairable artifacts. Standard validation remains koala validate --story=B-69bf plus the npm smoke commands.
expectedOutcome: Older projects with tracked .koala/activity.jsonl no longer make every Koala command stale materialHash evidence. Doctor points to safe repair, while real source, config, docs, and package changes still stale evidence.
actualTranscript: koala validate --story=B-69bf passed with npm test and 15/15 verification intents covered. test:verification-freshness-smoke, test:validation-protocol, test:entrypoints 23/23, verify-worktree-baseline-risk, runtime-fact-contract, build, and npm test all passed. Reviewer F-001 found an unsafe double-quoted repair snippet; it was fixed with POSIX single-quote escaping and a metacharacter regression.
outcomeDiff: No functional gap observed; F-001 was an extra review-discovered hardening issue and was fixed before DONE.
limitations: none - fully covered for CLI runtime artifact behavior; doctor --repair is explicit and does not run unless requested.
pitfalls: Initial review found shell metacharacter risk in the pasteable git rm command; evidence had to be refreshed after material commits because HEAD changed; runtime artifacts are intentionally separate from process-fact and runtime-fact registries.
